translations.text: “What use are your many sacrifices to me?” says the Lord. “I have had enough of burnt offerings of rams and the fat of fattened animals. I do not desire the blood of bulls, lambs, or goats.”
And against every high tower and every strong wall.
On that day he will answer and say, “I will not be a leader, for there is neither bread nor clothing in my house. Do not make me ruler over the people.”
Tell the righteous that it is good, for they will eat the fruit of their deeds.
There will be a shelter to give shade from the heat by day, and to provide cover and refuge from downpours and rain.
Now, men of Judah and inhabitants of Jerusalem, judge between me and my vineyard.
With harps and lyres and [?] and [?], they drink wine, but they do not consider the deeds of God or look at the work of his hands.

Therefore, as stubble is consumed by a tongue of fire that catches from an unleashed flame, they will be consumed. Their root will become like dust, and their shoots will rise like dust, because they rejected the law of the mighty Lord and provoked the word of the Holy One of Israel.
He will raise a banner for the nations far away and whistle for them from the ends of the earth, and they will come swiftly and speedily.
They will not grow weary or stumble; they will not doze or sleep. They will not loosen the belts around their waists, and the straps of their sandals will not break.
The Lord said to me, “Take a large scroll and write on it in ordinary handwriting: ‘Hasten the captivity and hurry the plunder.’”
He will be a sanctuary, a stone to strike against and a rock that causes stumbling for both houses of Israel, and snares and traps for the inhabitants of Jerusalem.
Here I am, with the children whom the Lord has given me, as a sign and a wonder in Israel from the mighty Lord, who dwells on Mount Zion.
This is what the mighty Lord says: “My people who dwell in Zion, do not fear the Assyrian who strikes you with his rod and raises his staff against you as Egypt did.”
The mighty Lord will raise a whip against him, like the blow against Midian on Mount Horeb. His staff will be over the sea, and he will lift it as he did against Egypt.

He will judge the poor truthfully and rebuke the evil people of the earth with justice. He will strike the earth with the rod of his mouth, and with the breath of his lips he will put the wicked to death.
The cow and the bear will graze together, and their young will lie down together. The lion will eat straw like the ox.
The Lord will dry up the tongue of the sea in Egypt and raise his hand over the river with the power of his wind. He will strike it into seven streams so that people can cross wearing sandals.
On that day you will say, “I thank you, Lord, because you were angry with me, but you turned away your anger and comforted me.”
Look, I trust in God my Savior and will not tremble, because the Lord is my strength and my praise, and he will be my salvation.
Raise a banner on the bare mountains. Raise your voice to them; wave your hand, so that rulers may enter your gates.
For the stars of heaven and their hosts will not shine. The sun will grow dark when it rises, and the light of the moon will not shine.
For the Lord has compassion on Jacob and will choose Israel again. He will settle them in their own land, and settlers will join them and be added to the house of Jacob.
You will take up this saying against the king of Babylon and say, “How the ruler has ceased, and the taskmaster has ceased!”
Even the cypresses and the cedars of Lebanon rejoice over you: “Since you lay down, no one has come up against us to cut us down.”
He made the world desolate like a wilderness, overthrew its towns, and did not release his prisoners.
They went up to the house of Ribon, to the high places, to weep. Moab wails over Nebo and Medeba. Every head has bald patches, and every beard is shaved.
For the waters of Nimrim will disappear, because the hay has dried up, the young grass has withered, and there is no greenery.
Therefore Moab will wail, and everyone will wail over Moab. You will groan like sick people over the foundations of the walls that have been demolished.
This is the word that the Lord spoke about Moab in earlier times.
All you inhabitants of the world who dwell on the earth, when a banner is raised on the mountains, you will see it; and when the trumpet sounds, you will hear it.
He saw a mounted company of two horsemen, a rider on a donkey and a rider on a camel, and he listened very carefully.
The pronouncement concerning the Valley of Vision. What is the matter with you here, that all of you have gone up to the rooftops?
The city is filled with turmoil; the strong city is filled with noise. Your slain were not killed by the sword, nor did they die in battle.
Look, the Lord will hurl you away, man, and make you wander far away.
Be ashamed, Sidon, for the sea, the stronghold of the sea, has said, “I have not been in labor or given birth; I have not raised young men or brought up young women.”
There is wailing over the wine in the streets. All joy has ceased, and the earth's gladness has passed away.
On that day this song will be sung in the land of Judah: “A city whose salvation is strong! Set up a wall and an outer wall.”
The wicked man has been removed, so that he may not learn righteousness. Rebuke is established in the land, and they will not see the Lord's majesty.
You have increased the nation, Lord; you have increased the nation. You have withdrawn and driven away all the ends of the earth.
On that day the Lord will thresh from the flow of the River to the stream of Egypt, and you, children of Israel, will be gathered one by one.
The proud crown of drunken Ephraim will be trampled underfoot.
The dishonored wreath, the strength of his glory, at the head of the fertile valley, will be like an early fig before summer: when someone sees it, he swallows it while it is still in his hand.

These too have gone astray through wine and gone astray through strong drink. Priests and prophets have gone astray through strong drink; they have been swallowed up by wine. They have staggered from strong drink, gone astray in drunkenness, and eaten extravagantly.
For all the tables are filled with vomit and filth, leaving no place clean.
I said to them, “This is my rest: give rest to the weary. This is quiet.” But they were unwilling to listen.
I will distress Ariel, and there will be groaning and lamentation, and she will be like Ariel.

Why are we turned upside down? You are considered like the potter's clay. Does the work say to its maker, “You did not make me,” or the thing formed say to the one who formed it, “You did not form me wisely”?
The Lord will give you bread in distress and water in distress. He will no longer gather your deceivers, and your eyes will see your deceivers.
Look, kings will rule in righteousness, and rulers will exercise authority with justice.
A man will be like a shelter from the wind, like a refuge from a rainstorm, like a stream of water in a thirsty place, and like the shade of a mighty rock in a weary land.
Justice will dwell in the wilderness, and righteousness will be bestowed in Carmel.
If he appears to them, they will wail loudly, and the messengers of peace will weep bitterly.
There the hedgehog nested, laid eggs, brooded, and hatched them in her shade. There the kites gathered, each with its mate.
Be strengthened, weak hands, and be made firm, trembling knees.
Then the eyes of the blind will be opened, and the ears of the deaf will be opened.
There will be a path there, and it will be called the Holy Way. No uncleanness will pass along it, and there will be no road on it. Fools will not wander there.
This is what the king says: Do not let Hezekiah deceive you, because he cannot rescue you.
When King Hezekiah heard this, he tore his clothes, covered himself with sackcloth, and entered the house of the Lord.
Isaiah said to them, “Say this to your master: This is what the Lord says: Do not be afraid of the words you have heard, with which the messengers of the king of Assyria have blasphemed me.”
Say this to Hezekiah, king of Judah: Do not let your God, in whom you trust, deceive you when you say that Jerusalem will not be handed over to the king of Assyria.
The writing of Hezekiah, king of Judah, when he became sick and recovered from his illness.

Look, the days are coming when everything in your house will be taken away, and the treasure your ancestors have accumulated until today will go to Babylon. Nothing will be left for you, says the Lord.
Whom did he consult, who taught him, made him understand the way of justice, taught him knowledge, and showed him the way of understanding?
He makes rulers nothing and the judges of the earth as though they did not exist.
I have been silent for a long time; I will keep silent. I have held back. Like a woman in labor, I will gasp and lay waste all at once.
I will say to the north, “Give them up,” and to the south, “Do not hold them back. Bring my sons from far away and my daughters from the ends of the earth.”
It becomes fuel for people: they take some of it, warm themselves, and bake bread. They also make a god and worship it; they make a carved image and bow down to it.
I have swept away your wrongdoing like mist and your sins like a cloud. Return to me, for I have redeemed you.
To whom have you likened me and compared me?
Remember these things and consider them; take your wrongdoings to heart.
I call a bird from the east, and from a distant land a man who will carry out my purpose. I have spoken, and I will bring it about. I have planned it, and I will do it.
I have brought my righteousness near to coming, and my salvation will not delay. I will give salvation in Zion and my glory to Israel.
Sit in [?]; enter the darkness, daughter of the Chaldeans, for they will no longer call you the mighty lady of kingdoms.
For they are named after the holy city and rely on the God of Israel; the Lord Almighty is his name.
Soon your children [?]; those who tore you down and destroyed you will leave you.
The children of your bereavement will again say in your hearing, “This place is too cramped for us. Make room for us to live.”
Listen to me, peoples, and pay attention to me, nations, because a law goes out from me, and my judgment is a light for the peoples.
My righteousness has drawn near, and my salvation has gone out. By my arm the peoples will be judged. The islands wait for me and put their hope in my arm.
For I put my words in your mouth and covered you with the shadow of my hands, when I stretched out the heavens and established the foundations of the earth and said to Zion, “You are my people.”
Shake off the dust and rise; sit down, Jerusalem. Untie the yoke from your neck, captive daughter of Zion.
The Lord has revealed his holy arm before the eyes of all the peoples, and all the ends of the earth will see the salvation of our God.
For you will not go out in haste, nor will you leave in flight, because the Lord goes before you, and the God of Israel gathers you together.
The Lord desired to humble him and make him suffer. A sin offering was laid upon his life, so that he might see offspring and prolong his days. The Lord’s will will prosper through his hand.
For your Lord does this for you; the mighty Lord is his name. Your Redeemer, the Holy One of Israel, will be called the God of the whole earth.
For the Lord has called you like an abandoned woman, distressed in spirit, and like a wife married in youth who is abandoned, says your God.
This is like the days of Noah to me: as I swore that the waters of Noah would never again pass over the earth, so I have sworn that I will not be angry with you or rebuke you.
Incline your ears and come to me. Listen to me, and your soul will live. I will establish an everlasting covenant with you, the sure mercies of David.
For you will go out with joy and depart in peace. The mountains and hills will rejoice before you with praise, and all the trees of the field will clap their hands.
On high and lofty mountains you made your bed, and you also went up there to offer sacrifices.
For I will not contend forever, nor will I be angry forever, because the spirit goes out from me, and I made the breath of life.
The wicked are troubled like the sea, because they cannot be still, and its waters toss up debris and mud.
Then your light will break forth like the dawn, and your righteousness will quickly shine out. Your righteousness will go before you, and the glory of the Lord will gather you together.

Those from among you will rebuild the ancient ruins, and you will raise up foundations from generation to generation. They will call you the one who closes breaches and restores paths for people to live along.
We feel our way along the wall like the blind; we grope like those who have no eyes. We stumble at noon as though it were evening, and we groan like those who are near death.

We have acted wickedly and dealt falsely with the Lord, and we have turned away from following our God. We have spoken oppression and rebelled; we have conceived and pondered words of falsehood in our hearts.
For look, darkness covers the earth, and thick darkness covers the nations. But the Lord will shine upon you, and his glory will be seen over you.
For the people and kingdom that will not serve you will perish, and the nations will be devastated by the sword.
The sun will no longer be your light by day, and the moon’s light will not shine for you, because the Lord will be your everlasting light.
Instead, those who gather it will eat it and praise the Lord, and those who gather it will drink it in the holy courts.
For the day of vengeance is in my heart, and the year of my deliverance has come.
And they melted as wax melts before fire. The fire will burn your enemies, and your name will be known to your enemies, and the nations will tremble before you.
There is no one who calls on your name or remembers to hold fast to you, because you have turned your face away from us and handed us over to our sins.
A sound of turmoil from the city, a sound from the temple—the voice of the Lord, who brings retribution upon his enemies.
